newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Thursday with three new domestic A shares listed today attracting much liquidity from the repo market, traders said.
The annual rate for the shortest three-day contract rose slightly to 37.4 percent from an already very high rate of 36.5 percent on Wednesday.
Traders said the contract became a very hot bidding target because the Chinese lunar new year holiday starting next Monday will postpone the maturity date of this contract to February 18.
The market will close from February 3 to 17 on the holiday.
But the annual rate for the most active 28-day contract bucked the trend and fell to 9.65 percent from 9.80 percent.
One trader said financial institutions favoured trading the 28-day contract because of its comparatively low rate.
Combined turnover of the six-contract market rose to 2.75 million lots from 2.64 million lots. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said a holiday mood ahead of the Chinese lunar new year prevailed in the market and the rates were likely to move down on Friday in light trading.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up, continuing a technical rebound starting on Wednesday after heavy losses in the last few weeks, traders said.
The most active three-year note that matures in Oct 1999, rose to 103.27 yuan from 103.09 yuan on Wednesday.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 1.03 million lots from 1.1 million lots.
Traders said they expected the spot contracts to fall sharply on profit-taking on Friday, the last trading day before the Chinese lunar new year.
